payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly show a frog placed inside the toilet bowl?
node.criteria: Pass if a frog is clearly visible within the toilet bowl; fail if the image clearly shows no frog inside the bowl; unknown if the bowl or its contents are obscured or the evidence is otherwise insufficient to determine this.
node.binding: The frog must be inside the toilet bowl of the toilet in the input image.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The edited image visibly shows a frog within the toilet bowl, so the completion evidence supports yes; the reference partial label alone does not establish that this is wrong. However, the trace’s near-certain yes conflicts with the supplied partial reference, and its evidence is internally overbroad: it says frogs are on the lid and nearby, while the image shows frogs on the raised seat and floor as well as one in the bowl. Improve the node’s binding/criteria so completion is judged from the frog’s actual spatial relation to the bowl—not mere proximity or presence elsewhere—and make the completion and progress checks distinguish those cases consistently. Investigate why the reference is partial rather than forcing that label: the image appears to contain a frog inside the bowl, so the discrepancy may reflect an ambiguous completion criterion or reference, not absent progress. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; both supports were queried and passed. Treat the 0.99 confidence as a calibration signal to review, not as evidence against the visible bowl placement.
s2: The node’s question and criteria conflict: it asks whether there is progress even if the frog is not inside the bowl, but the trace treats a frog clearly inside as partial progress. Make this support check classify only incomplete, visible movement toward the bowl as partial progress; explicitly distinguish frogs on the raised seat/lid or floor (nearby but not progress by themselves) from a frog whose body is visibly within the bowl, which is completion evidence for the separate fulfillment check. Bind the judgment to the frog’s spatial relation to the bowl, not mere proximity or other frogs elsewhere, and keep the completion and progress criteria mutually consistent. The edited image visibly includes a frog inside the bowl, alongside frogs on the raised seat and floor, so do not infer that the requested edit is absent or force the reference’s partial label; investigate the reference/criterion discrepancy. The 0.99 confidence merits calibration review, but is not contrary visual evidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
